chapters.title: Search & Retrieval · Evaluation: Reading Guide
chapters.description: A complete evaluation sequence: define relevance, compute ranking metrics, diagnose pipeline stages, estimate uncertainty, and validate user outcomes.

chapters.title: Search Evaluation Starts with Relevance, Not a Metric
chapters.description: Build query sets and relevance judgments, handle incomplete labels, and prevent temporal and entity leakage before computing a score.

chapters.title: Precision, Recall, MAP, and MRR: One Ranking, Four Questions
chapters.description: Compute every metric by hand, distinguish AP from precision, state AP@K conventions, and explore rankings directly.

chapters.title: nDCG: How Much Does the Order of Useful Results Matter?
chapters.description: Derive DCG and nDCG with graded relevance, compare gain functions, and separate ranking quality from diversity and catalog coverage.

chapters.title: Evaluate Retrieval and Reranking Separately
chapters.description: Distinguish ANN recall from relevance recall, calculate a candidate-set ceiling, and diagnose losses at each search stage.

chapters.title: Did Search Improve? Paired Tests, Bootstrap Intervals, and Slices
chapters.description: Estimate uncertainty over queries, preserve pairing, handle repeated users, and distinguish statistical evidence from product significance.

chapters.title: Clicks Are Feedback, Not Relevance Labels
chapters.description: Understand position bias, exposure, inverse propensity weighting, randomized experiments, and the gap between offline ranking gains and user outcomes.

chapters.title: RAG Evaluation: Find the Evidence, Use It, and Cite It
chapters.description: Separate evidence retrieval, context construction, answer correctness, faithfulness, citation quality, and abstention with controlled counterfactuals.
